args.reason: The old decision forbids writing secrets anywhere under .faff/, not only committing them. The new decision writes literal resolved API keys to .faff/cache/credentials.json in plaintext, which is exactly what the rule prohibits. Being gitignored stops the file reaching the repo but does nothing about local exposure, backups, cage or sandbox mounts, or other tools that read .faff/. The justification is also weak: reading process.env is an in-memory lookup, and if repeated reads mattered an in-process cache would give the same gain without putting anything on disk. The rationale for the old rule still holds, so the supersession argument is unsound.
